arguments.summary: A critical firewall integrity alert was triggered by suspicious activity originating from host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42), a high-criticality finance department endpoint. Investigation confirmed Cobalt Strike beaconing to a known malicious C2 server (198.51.100.23:443) via rundll32.exe and DNS tunneling activity. The host exhibited multiple MITRE ATT&CK techniques including T1071.001 (Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols), T1218.011 (Signed Binary Proxy Execution: Rundll32), T1566.001 (Phishing: Spearphishing Attachment), and T1565.001 (Data Manipulation: Stored Data Manipulation). The user account jsmith@corp.local was successfully revoked to prevent lateral movement. No malicious code was found in the extracted payload, but behavioral indicators confirm compromise. The firewall and EPP actions were blocked due to consensus failure.

arguments.summary: A critical compromise was detected on workstation WS-FIN-042 (IP: 10.0.5.42), attributed to a phishing-induced Cobalt Strike beacon. The host exhibited C2 communication with a known malicious IP (198.51.100.23) via rundll32.exe, attempted lateral movement via SMB, and executed encoded PowerShell. The user account 'jsmith@corp.local' was compromised. Immediate containment actions included password and MFA reset, host isolation, and execution of a remediation playbook. No data exfiltration to the primary C2 was confirmed, but the incident represents a high-risk intrusion attempt targeting the Finance department.

arguments.summary: A Golden Ticket attack was confirmed within the CORP domain, originating from the compromise of the krbtgt account. The initial access vector was a Cobalt Strike beacon deployed on workstation WS-FIN-042 (user jsmith). The attacker performed lateral movement via SMB, attempted Kerberos TGT forgery, and ultimately exfiltrated the krbtgt hash, enabling the creation of persistent, undetectable forged domain tickets. As a result, all Domain Admin accounts were considered compromised, necessitating a full credential revocation and krbtgt password reset cycle.

        description = "Detects Cobalt Strike beaconing over HTTPS via JA3 fingerprint and URI pattern"

        severity = "critical"
    strings:
        $s1 = "GET / HTTP/1.1" nocase
        $s2 = "Host:" fullword nocase
        $s3 = "Connection: Keep-Alive" fullword nocase
        $re_uri = /^\/\w{4,8}\/\w{8,12}\/\w{4,8}\/\w{8,12}\/\w{4,8}$/
    condition:
        all of ($s*) or $re_uri
}

arguments.summary: A Golden Ticket attack was confirmed following the compromise of the Kerberos krbtgt account hash, leading to the forgery of valid TGTs. The initial access vector was a phishing campaign that delivered a Cobalt Strike beacon via malicious Office macro to user CORP\jsmith on host WS-FIN-042. The attacker performed lateral movement via SMB and attempted Kerberos TGT requests, triggering alerts. The EDR and IDS detected C2 beacons and suspicious PowerShell activity. A full credential compromise of all Domain Admins was confirmed, necessitating mass credential revocation and krbtgt password resets. The host was remediated using an automated playbook, and all active sessions were invalidated.

rule CobaltStrike_Beacon_Pattern {
    meta:
        description = "Detects memory patterns typical of Cobalt Strike beacons"
        author = "SOC Team"
        reference = "https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0154/"
        maltype = "backdoor"
    strings:
        $a = { 2e 72 63 64 2e 65 78 65 } // ".rcd.exe"
        $b = "implant_get" wide ascii
        $c = { 00 00 00 00 01 00 00 00 [4] 00 00 00 00 } // Beacon config header
    condition:
        all of them
}

arguments.summary: A Golden Ticket attack was confirmed against the corp.local domain, originating from a compromised finance workstation (WS-FIN-042). The attacker used Cobalt Strike for initial C2 communication, performed lateral movement via SMB, and successfully exfiltrated the krbtgt account hash. This allowed the forging of Kerberos TGTs, leading to the compromise of all 15 Domain Admin accounts. Immediate actions included mass credential revocation, krbtgt password reset, full system scans, and host hardening.

IDS alerts triggered for Cobalt Strike beaconing activity (ET TROJAN signature).
Failed Kerberos TGT request from WS-FIN-042, indicating potential Kerberoasting or Golden Ticket misuse.
Lateral movement observed via SMB to internal file server (10.0.5.50).
Mass credential compromise alert generated; incident officially declared.
EPP full scan completed on WS-FIN-042; Dropper.Linux.Agent.F detected in cron directory.
Golden Ticket attack confirmed via Kerberos TGT analysis. 15 Domain Admin accounts identified as compromised.
Mass credential revocation initiated: all 15 Domain Admin accounts disabled, passwords reset, sessions revoked.
krbtgt account password reset twice to invalidate all forged tickets.
Windows workstation hardening playbook applied to WS-FIN-042.

  timeframe: 24h
falsepositives:

level: high

arguments.summary: Critical zero-day vulnerability (ZD-2026-EDR-001) identified in EDR agent kernel driver (edrsensor.sys), enabling unauthenticated remote code execution at SYSTEM level. The vulnerability affects all 2,847 endpoints running EDR agent version 12.4.1. The initial alert was triggered on host WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15), which also exhibited prior network scanning activity and was found to be infected with cryptocurrency miner malware. Immediate actions included resetting credentials for the associated helpdesk user and issuing a global directive to disable the vulnerable EDR agent service pending patch availability.

Critical EDR vulnerability alert triggered on host 10.0.10.50 (mapped to WS-IT-101).
Cryptocurrency miner (Miner.CoinHive.A) detected and quarantined on WS-IT-101 during full endpoint scan.
Password and MFA token for user CORP\helpdesk reset as precautionary measure.
Global advisory issued to disable EDR agent service (EDRSensor) on all 2,847 endpoints due to active exploitation of zero-day RCE vulnerability.

Investigation revealed prior low-severity IDS alerts indicating network scanning behavior originating from this IP. The host (WS-IT-101) was confirmed to be an internal IT workstation running Ubuntu. A firewall rule was successfully implemented to block outbound traffic from the IP, and the associated user account (CORP\helpdesk) had its credentials and MFA reset as a precaution. No malicious processes, files, or lateral movement were observed during EDR queries. The incident was contained without escalation.

arguments.summary: A critical storage failure alert was triggered from host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42), which was found to be compromised with Cobalt Strike beaconing activity. The host exhibited multiple malicious behaviors including encoded PowerShell execution, unsigned DLL loading via rundll32, outbound C2 communication over HTTPS, and host file modification. A suspicious PowerShell script was identified that performs dynamic code execution and downloads a remote payload. Despite detection, containment actions (firewall block, EPP quarantine, IAM lockout, Ansible remediation) were blocked due to lack of consensus. The destination host (10.0.9.25) showed no signs of compromise.

rule Suspicious_PowerShell_Download
{
    meta:
        description = "Detects PowerShell script downloading remote payload via WebClient"
        author = "SOC Team"
        reference = "MITRE ATT&CK T1105"
        date = "2026-04-09"
    strings:
        $webclient = "New-Object Net.WebClient" wide ascii
        $download = "DownloadData" wide ascii
        $invoke = "Invoke-Expression" wide ascii
    condition:
        all of them
}

arguments.summary: Critical SIEM storage failure detected during investigation of a compromised host (WS-FIN-042). Host exhibited signs of Cobalt Strike beaconing, encoded PowerShell execution, and lateral movement attempts. Concurrently, the SIEM hot storage array (10.0.9.25) is failing, with 847 GB of critical forensic logs at risk of permanent loss. Emergency log export was recommended but not executed due to consensus denial. A full EPP scan identified a Linux dropper, though its relevance is under review.

Critical alert: SIEM hot storage array (10.0.9.25) in degraded state with imminent data loss (estimated 23 minutes).
Recommendation issued to perform emergency log export to //10.0.15.200/emergency-siem-backup.
Emergency log export and firewall isolation actions denied by consensus.
Full EPP scan of WS-FIN-042 completed, detecting 'Dropper.Linux.Agent.F' in a non-Windows context; further analysis required.

arguments.summary: A critical compromise was identified on workstation WS-FIN-042 (IP: 10.0.5.42), initially triggered by a Cobalt Strike beacon connecting to a known C2 server (198.51.100.23). The source IP in the emergency access alert (10.0.5.14) was a misattribution; the actual compromised host was 10.0.5.42. Lateral movement via SMB to a file server was detected. Emergency containment actions included blocking the C2 IP at the firewall, resetting the user's credentials and MFA, deploying a full endpoint scan which detected a Linux dropper (likely a false positive or secondary payload), and applying a hardening playbook. A CrowdStrike IR consultant was granted time-limited Domain Admin and Schema Admin privileges for forensic investigation.

Firewall rule deployed to block outbound traffic to C2 IP 198.51.100.23 from 10.0.5.42.
User 'CORP\jsmith' credentials and MFA reset. Secure enrollment link sent.
CrowdStrike IR consultant granted temporary Domain Admin and Schema Admin privileges via PAM.
Full endpoint scan on WS-FIN-042 completed, detecting 'Dropper.Linux.Agent.F' in a non-standard location.
Hardening playbook 'workstation_lockdown.yml' successfully applied to WS-FIN-042.

        CommandLine|contains: 
            - '%TEMP%'
            - '%AppData%'
            - '%LocalAppData%'
    condition: selection
level: high
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0194/
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate software updates (rare)
author: SOC Team

arguments.summary: A compromised finance workstation (WS-FIN-042) was used as an initial access point by an attacker leveraging Cobalt Strike beaconing to a known C2 server. The attacker attempted lateral movement via SMB and Kerberos exploitation. Emergency access was granted to a CrowdStrike IR consultant for forensic response. The source IP (10.0.5.14) was blocked at the firewall, and the affected host was scanned and found to host a Linux-based dropper, indicating potential cross-platform malware presence.

timeline.description: Initial outbound HTTPS connection from WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42) to suspicious IP 198.51.100.23.
Suspicious rundll32 execution detected on WS-FIN-042, likely payload activation.
IDS alerts on Cobalt Strike beaconing activity (ET TROJAN signature).
Failed Kerberos TGT request from WS-FIN-042, indicating potential credential abuse or brute-force attempt.
Successful SMB access to internal file server (10.0.5.50), confirming lateral movement.
Emergency access request submitted for IR engagement.
Firewall rule deployed to block outbound traffic to 10.0.5.14.
Full EPP scan of WS-FIN-042 completed; detected 'Dropper.Linux.Agent.F' in cron job directory.
User jsmith@corp.local password and MFA reset; secure enrollment link issued.
Privileged access granted to temp_contractor_42 with Domain Admins and Schema Admins membership for 72 hours under PAM-2026-EMER-0094.

arguments.summary: A critical compromise was initiated via a phishing-induced Cobalt Strike beacon on a high-criticality finance workstation (WS-FIN-042). The attacker performed lateral movement via SMB and attempted Kerberos exploitation. Emergency access was granted to an IR consultant for containment and forensic analysis. The compromised host was isolated, and credentials for user CORP\jsmith were reset. A Linux dropper was also identified on the same host via cross-platform malware.

timeline.description: Initial outbound HTTPS connection to known Cobalt Strike C2 server (198.51.100.23) from WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42).
Suspicious rundll32 execution detected from Temp directory on WS-FIN-042.
IDS alerts on Cobalt Strike beacon C2 activity (ET TROJAN signature).
Failed Kerberos TGT request from WS-FIN-042, indicating potential credential misuse or brute-force attempt.
Lateral movement detected via SMB access to file server (10.0.5.50).
Emergency privileged access request submitted for CrowdStrike IR consultant (temp_contractor_42).
IP 10.0.5.14 blocked at firewall for C2 communication.
User CORP\jsmith password and MFA token reset; secure enrollment link issued.
Domain Admin and Schema Admin privileges granted to temp_contractor_42 for 72 hours.
Full EPP scan detects Dropper.Linux.Agent.F on WS-FIN-042.
Workstation lockdown playbook applied to WS-FIN-042 (registry, service, and firewall hardening).
